title: Renewal & expansion check-in - Solis Health
next_steps: Send updated pricing for dedicated pool + extra region (Avery) - by 2026-04-02
Share SOC2/ISO artifacts and network diagram (Marcus) - by 2026-04-01
Schedule 1-hour benchmark run with Solis test harness (Marcus + Lina) - target week of 2026-04-05
Draft 6-month contract extension with option to convert to annual reserved capacity (Avery) - by 2026-04-03
action_items: Avery Chen - prepare pricing deck with committed monthly GPU hours and EU region add-on - 2026-04-02
Marcus Lee - run baseline latency/throughput benchmark using Solis test harness (50 RPS mixed) and upload results - 2026-04-07
Lina Patel - provide sample traffic profile and peak window details to Redwood - 2026-04-01
summary: Solis Health is entering renewal conversation. They want to extend contract 6 months with option for annual reserved capacity. Primary asks: add EU region, increase dedicated GPU pool by ~30%, confirm SOC2 + network controls, and run a benchmark to validate latency at 50 RPS. Redwood to send updated pricing and SOC2 artifacts; schedule benchmark.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana (Solis): Dana here, Rashid and Lina with me.
[00:12] Rashid (Solis): hi, thanks for setting up.
[00:15] Marcus (Redwood): Marcus from Redwood on the infra side.
[00:18] Avery (Redwood): Cool, agenda — renewal status, capacity needs, EU region ask, security docs, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:26] Dana: Yep. Rashid wants to start with the capacity ask.
[00:30] Rashid: Yeah, our traffic is up ~35% q/q, and we're hitting the committed pool more often. We want to talk about bumping dedicated capacity by about 30% and also adding an EU region so our European clinics get sub-200ms p99.
[00:45] Marcus: Got it. Quick clarification — is the 30% permanent or burst during peak hours?
[00:50] Rashid: Mostly permanent. Peak windows still matter but baseline has moved up. We do have some very spiky windows at 9–11am UTC.
[00:57] Lina: Also we have data residency concerns for EU patients; need to ensure model inference for EU traffic stays in eu-west.
[01:05] Avery: Totally understandable. We can do regional routing and a dedicated pool in eu-west, or run a second dedicated pool with pinning. There's some tradeoffs on cost and cross-region KV cache misses.
[01:20] Dana: Can you explain the KV cache thing again? We've heard different descriptions.
[01:25] Marcus: Sure, so if you split pools by region, the KV cache (prefix caching, conversational context) won't be shared across regions, which can increase token compute for cross-region users. For EU-only traffic that's fine. For users who move across regions occasionally we'd expect slight latency/cost impact if context isn't warm.
[01:41] Rashid: Hmm, ok, most of our EU users are EU-only so that's fine. The bigger question is pricing. We were looking at reserved capacity but are nervous about lock-in. Can we do a 6-month extension with option to convert to annual reserved?
[01:56] Avery: We can do a bridging commit — 6 months at a slightly discounted rate with a conversion clause to annual reserved capacity. I'll draft terms.
[02:05] Dana: For compliance — we need SOC2 Type II report plus details on audit logs and KMS integration. Also SSO/SAML and RBAC for team separation.
[02:17] Marcus: We have SOC2 + network diagram ready to share; KMS integrations supported for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can integrate customer-managed keys for Private. I'll share the artifact.
[02:31] Lina: Are audit logs retained long-term? We need at least 1 year of immutable logs for certain cases.
[02:36] Marcus: Audit retention can be configured; for Dedicated and Private we can extend retention and provide a log export. Will include in the doc.
[02:44] Rashid: Performance — our SLA target is p99 < 200ms for short prompts, but currently we're seeing p99 ~ 220ms on some routes. We need to validate if increased capacity and EU region will bring that down.
[02:57] Marcus: Agree. We'll run an end-to-end benchmark using your harness at 50 RPS mixed load and measure p50/p95/p99. Expect improvements with dedicated scaling and local region routing.
[03:10] Avery: What's your timeline for a decision?
[03:12] Dana: Ideally by mid-April. Our current contract ends 2026-05-01, so we want renewal terms in place two weeks before.
[03:20] Avery: Ok, so target sign by 2026-04-17. We'll aim to get pricing and docs to you in the next week.
[03:26] Rashid: One more thing — competitor pricing. Anthropic and Vertex proposals are on the table; Anthropic's managed offering was cheaper for token costs but less predictable latency.
[03:36] Avery: Noted. We can include cost-per-p99 projection for the proposed config so you can compare unit economics.
[03:42] Dana: Great.
[03:45] Marcus: Quick technical note — if you want sub-200ms p99 in eu-west with large context windows, we recommend the dedicated pool with batching tuned to short-latency mode and prefix caching enabled. We'll provide suggested config.
[03:59] Lina: For the benchmark, can we include some of our longer prompts (5–8k tokens) to see effects on kv cache and latency?
[04:06] Marcus: Yes, include representative payloads; large context will influence latency significantly. We'll capture token breakdowns in the report.
[04:15] Rashid: About routing — do you have graceful fallback if eu-west is overloaded? We can't have endpoints fail for clinic traffic.
[04:23] Avery: Yes, Smart routing can fail over to a compatible variant in another region, but we'd prefer to configure burst capacity in eu-west as first line. We'll propose burst policy.
[04:33] Dana: Ok. Also legal asked about contractual data residency language — can we add a clause that EU traffic will be processed in eu-west for specified endpoints?
[04:42] Avery: Yes, that's possible for specific routes. I'll work with legal to draft language.
[04:48] Rashid: On metrics — can Redwood expose token-level cost and latency per route in the console so we can watch spend?
[04:55] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route breakdowns and tracing hooks; we can show you dashboards and set up alerts for spend and latency.
[05:03] Dana: Sounds good.
[05:05] Avery: Recap of action items: I'll send pricing + conversion clause, Marcus will share SOC2 & network diagrams and run benchmark, Lina will share traffic profile, and we'll target sign mid-April. Anything else?
[05:18] Rashid: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[05:20] Marcus: Thanks.
[47:58] [call ends]
